note: DEFECT-2 BUGFIX, NOT NEW COVERAGE (restated at the prior claim's exact number — this line was already counted, just wrongly implemented). Sweep() cast its anti-tunneling ray from `b.Obj.position` (the body's CURRENT, already-moved position — Step() sets `_prevPos = Obj.position; Obj.position += Vel * dt;` and only THEN calls Sweep, see Step()'s own comment) where src/planephys.js:871 `this.ray.set(b.prev, dir)` casts from the PREVIOUS position. Casting from the current position defeats the sweep's whole purpose: a wall that sat between last step's spot and this step's spot ends up BEHIND the body relative to its direction of travel, so a forward-cast ray from the current position can never find it — a fast wreck tunnels through thin geometry between sub-steps. Fixed to `World.RaycastWorld(b.Prev, dir, maxDist, out hit)`. Confirmed b.Prev (LooseAirframeActor.Prev / `_prevPos`) IS correctly maintained: it is written at the top of EVERY Step() call, before the position move, so it already held the right value — the bug was purely in Sweep() reading the wrong field, nothing needed fixing in how Prev itself is kept.
verified: Unity -batchmode -quit -executeMethod TbilisiFly.Probes.SweepOriginProbe.Run -> SWEEPORIGIN ... originMatchesPrev=true originMatchesPost=false distOriginToPost=1.101262 (log: /tmp/sweeporigin.log) — new probe hands PlanePhysicsSystem a StubWorld whose RaycastWorld only records the `origin` argument it was called with, then shows that origin equals the body's own Prev (pre-move) and differs by >1 m from its post-move Obj.position in the same Update(dt) call. Regression-checked against LooseWreckProbe.Run (FALL/HIT lines unchanged) and PlanePhysicsProbe.Run (SOLVE/DAMAGE/RESTITUTION unchanged, untouched by this fix). Full project compiled clean.
